brief: UBS's 28-Oct cash trading note covers four themes. Markets: EStoxx dipped while US indices firmed (S&P +60bps, Nasdaq +1.2%) and Asian chip names rallied, Korea's KOSPI up about 7% to its best day in three months after SK Hynix's blowout Q3 print and roughly $45bn capital return, with Samsung +8%; Taiwan's TAIEX rose about 2% on OpenAI/Oracle/Google partnership news lifting MediaTek and TSMC, which is also reported lifting packaging prices 20% on AI demand. Crude rose 1.5-2% on a WSJ report of US-Gulf military preparations after the midterms. UBS expects sentiment to keep recovering into tonight's GOOG and MSFT earnings. FOMC: UBS's base case is a 10-2 hold tonight, Warsh hawkish, pause driven by midterm proximity and sticky ~3% inflation rather than overheating, then 25bp hikes in December and January, matching market pricing. UK Budget: UBS Economics expects a cautious budget as headroom fell from £23.6bn to about £10bn, rebuilding to roughly £15bn via smaller taxes while deferring welfare and spending cuts to 2027; gilts and GBP are seen supported, equities only selectively attractive, and a bank levy rise to 6-8% would cut NWG/LLOY 3-4% and BARC/HSBC 1-2%. Flow: Tuesday finished better-to-buy (54/46), led by Tech, Industrials and Banks on the bid, Healthcare and Energy demand against supply in Telecoms, Food & Bev, Utilities and Insurance.
